query: Casting is the predominant fabrication method for high-entropy alloys, but solidification-related porosity and microstructural nonuniformity can cause heterogeneous properties. Studies of other high-entropy-alloy compositions have reported high hardness and notable compressive performance, yet these findings do not establish how to improve CoCrFeNiTi; moreover, some investigated alloys were brittle at 25 °C and displayed only limited plastic deformation at 600 °C. For equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi with a simple crystal structure, favorable plasticity and machinability, but low hardness and load-bearing capability, what single intervention could improve hardness and mechanical performance while preserving those favorable characteristics and clarifying the relationship between microstructure and deformation? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, a quantitative prediction relative to the unmodified alloy, the processing and testing boundaries within which it should apply, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled microstructural and mechanical experiment with explicit falsification criteria.

generation.hypothesis: Introduction of a controlled amount of carbon to form carbides can enhance hardness and mechanical performance in CoCrFeNiTi high-entropy alloys while preserving favorable plasticity and machinability.
generation.material_initial_state: Equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi with a simple crystal structure
generation.intervention: Addition of carbon to form carbides
generation.conditions: Processing and testing within boundaries of temperature (25 °C to 600 °C) and strain rates relevant to mechanical performance evaluation
generation.mechanism: Pinning of dislocations by carbide precipitates, leading to increased strength and hardness
generation.predicted_outcome: An increase in hardness by at least 15% and improvement in compressive yield strength by 20% compared to the unmodified alloy, without significant loss in ductility
generation.baseline: Unmodified equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi alloy
generation.boundary: Temperature range of 25 °C to 600 °C and strain rates up to 10^-3 s^-1
generation.uncertainty: The optimal amount of carbon addition and the precise role of carbide distribution on mechanical properties

falsification_experiment.design: Controlled addition of carbon to CoCrFeNiTi alloys followed by microstructural characterization and mechanical testing
measurements: Compressive testing to determine yield strength and strain to failure
Microstructural analysis (SEM, TEM) to quantify carbide distribution and dislocation density
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the addition of carbon does not result in a significant increase in hardness and compressive yield strength without compromising ductility, the hypothesis is falsified.
